blocks.text: The desktop includes an SSH client. An SSH server is profile controlled and can use a nonstandard port and restricted source networks/users. Ask the administrator for the intended host, port and key fingerprint.

Replace PORT, USER and HOST deliberately. Verify the first host-key fingerprint through a trusted channel. A changed key can mean a rebuilt host or an interception attempt; investigate before removing known_hosts entries.

Client preferences live in ~/.ssh/config and known hosts in ~/.ssh/known_hosts. Server policy is installed under /etc/ssh/. Keep private keys and configuration private. If access is refused, check the actual configured port and allowed network through the managed tools before changing firewall or server policy.
Never paste private keys, passwords, authentication codes or agent contents into diagnostics. Do not enable root/password SSH as a workaround.
